claims.text: What the image looks like Buzzword: punched-out lytic lesions on skull XR → MM
claims.quote: Punched-out lytic lesions Skull X-ray Multiple myeloma

claims.text: Ex skull radiograph: multi, punched-out lesions in the bone, typical of MM
claims.quote: This skull radiograph shows multiple, punched-out lesions in the bone (arrows), which are typical of multiple myeloma.

claims.text: Skeletal survey (plain radiographs of skull, long bones, spine, pelvis, and ribs): punched-out lytic lesions or diffuse osteoporosis = present in ≈ 80% of cases
claims.quote: Radiographs include a skeletal survey (ie, plain radiographs of skull, long bones, spine, pelvis, and ribs). Punched-out lytic lesions or diffuse osteoporosis is present in approximately 80% of cases (3).

claims.text: Radionuclide bone scans USU are ⍉helpful; whole-body MRI can provide more detail and = obtained if specific sites of pain or neuro Sx are present; PET-CT provides prognostic info and can help determine whether pts have solitary plasmacytoma or MM
claims.quote: Radionuclide bone scans usually are not helpful. Whole-body MRI can provide more detail and is obtained if specific sites of pain or neurologic symptoms are present. PET-CT scans provide prognostic information and can help determine whether patients have solitary plasmacytoma or multiple myeloma.

claims.text: Aspects (abnorm in red) Diffuse osteoporosis or discrete osteolytic lesions are often present; MC sites are the pelvis, spine, ribs, femur, humerus, and skull
claims.quote: Diffuse osteoporosis or discrete osteolytic lesions are often present, with the most common sites being the pelvis, spine, ribs, femur, humerus, and skull.

claims.text: The osteolytic lesions are USU multi; occasionally they are solitary intramedullary masses
claims.quote: The osteolytic lesions are usually multiple; occasionally, they are solitary intramedullary masses.

claims.text: Labs: anemia in 80% of pts, USU normocytic, normochromic, w rouleaux (stacks of 3 to 12 RBC); WBC and platelet counts USU norm; BUN, creatinine, LDH, beta-2 microglobulin, and uric acid may be ↑; AG sometimes ↓; hypercalcemia @ dx in about 10%
claims.quote: Anemia is present in 80% of patients, usually a normocytic, normochromic anemia with formation of rouleaux (clusters of 3 to 12 red blood cells that occur in stacks) (3). White blood cell and platelet counts are usually normal. BUN, serum creatinine, LDH, beta-2 microglobulin, and serum uric acid may be elevated. The anion gap is sometimes low. Hypercalcemia is present at diagnosis in about 10% of patients.

claims.text: Eti A CA of plasma cells that prod monoclonal Ig and invade and destroy adjacent bone tissue
claims.quote: Multiple myeloma is a cancer of plasma cells that produce monoclonal immunoglobulin and invade and destroy adjacent bone tissue.

claims.text: Mech of the bone lesions: bone replace by expanding plasmacytomas, or cytokines secreted by malig plasma cells that activate osteoclasts and suppress osteoblasts, leading to bone loss
claims.quote: Lesions are caused by bone replacement by expanding plasmacytomas or by cytokines that are secreted by malignant plasma cells that activate osteoclasts and suppress osteoblasts, leading to bone loss.

claims.text: Median age = about 70 years; prevalence in Black people = twice that in White people; slight male predominance; Eti unknown, although chromosomal and genetic factors, radiation, and chemicals have been suggested
claims.quote: The median age is about 70 years. Prevalence in Black people is twice that in White people. There is a slight male predominance. The etiology is unknown, although chromosomal and genetic factors, radiation, and chemicals have been suggested.

claims.text: Sx Persistent bone pain (esp in the back or thorax), renal failure, and recurr bact infections are the MC problems on presentation; many pts are identified when routine tests show ↑total blood protein, proteinuria, or unexplained anemia or renal failure
claims.quote: Persistent bone pain (especially in the back or thorax), renal failure, and recurrent bacterial infections are the most common problems on presentation, but many patients are identified when routine laboratory tests show an elevated total protein level in the blood, proteinuria, or unexplained anemia or renal failure.

claims.text: Pathologic (fragility) fractures are common, and vertebral collapse may lead to spinal cord compress and paraplegia
claims.quote: Pathologic (fragility) fractures (ie, fractures that occur with minimal or no trauma) are common, and vertebral collapse may lead to spinal cord compression and paraplegia.

claims.text: Sus in pts > 40 years w persistent unexplained bone pain (particularly @ night or @ rest), other typical Sx, unexplained lab abnormalities (eg, ↑blood or urinary protein, hypercalcemia, renal insuff, anemia), or radiographs showing a pathologic frx or lytic lesions
claims.quote: Multiple myeloma is suspected in patients > 40 years with persistent unexplained bone pain, particularly at night or at rest, other typical symptoms, unexplained laboratory abnormalities (eg, elevated blood protein or urinary protein, hypercalcemia, renal insufficiency, anemia), or radiographs showing a pathologic fracture or lytic lesions.

claims.text: Tx and next step Next step: SPEP and UPEP followed by immunofixation, quantitative immunoglobulins, and serum free light chains
claims.quote: Do serum and urine protein electrophoresis followed by immunofixation, quantitative immunoglobulins, and measurement of serum free light chains.

claims.text: Next step: bone marrow aspiration and bx
claims.quote: Do bone marrow aspiration and biopsy.

claims.text: Pts w Sx and those w organ dysfun should be treated w pharmacotherapy, which may incl corticosteroids, chemo agents, proteasome inhibitors, immunomodulatory agents, monoclonal antibodies, selective inhibitors of nuclear export, histone deacetylase inhibitors, and cellular and antibody-based immune therapies targeting B-cell maturation Ag
claims.quote: Patients with symptoms and those with organ dysfunction should be treated with pharmacotherapy, which may include corticosteroids, chemotherapy agents, proteasome inhibitors, immunomodulatory agents, monoclonal antibodies, selective inhibitors of nuclear export, histone deacetylase inhibitors, and cellular and antibody-based immune therapies targeting B-cell maturation antigen.

claims.text: Stem cell transplantation = an option for some pts, but highly effective pharmacotherapy options may make it unnecessary in others
claims.quote: Stem cell transplantation is an option for some patients, but highly effective pharmacotherapy options may make it unnecessary in others.

claims.text: Possibly radiation therapy to specific Sxtomatic areas that do ⍉respond to systemic therapy
claims.quote: Possibly radiation therapy to specific symptomatic areas that do not respond to systemic therapy

claims.text: Tx of comp, eg, anemia, hypercalcemia, kidney dysfun, infections, and bone dz
claims.quote: Treatment of complications, eg, anemia, hypercalcemia, kidney dysfunction, infections, and bone disease
